processing: Little is documented specifically. As with other Japanese black teas, leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, usually by small makers.
harvest_season: Not well recorded for this tea. Japanese black teas are commonly picked in spring and summer, and the packet usually says which.
appearance_dry: Typical of Japanese black tea, dark twisted leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Japanese black tea, a clear amber-red.
appearance_wet: Typical of Japanese black tea, soft coppery leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for Yame black tea as a group; Japanese black teas are generally soft, gently sweet and low in astringency.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Japanese black tea. It takes well to a shorter first steep and a longer second.

vintage_note: As is usual for Japanese black tea, it is sold in small lots by harvest year and season, often naming the grower and cultivar. Look for the current or previous year, since these teas are made to be drunk fresh, not aged.
description:
Yame Koucha simply means black tea from Yame, in Fukuoka Prefecture. It is a place name on a packet rather than a tightly defined style, and little is documented about it as a group.

As with other Japanese black teas, makers wither, roll, oxidise and dry the leaf in small quantities, so each grower's tea can differ noticeably.

The class usually tastes soft and lightly sweet, without the grip of an Assam. Water just off the boil and a modest steep suit it better than a long, hard brew.

When buying, read the label for grower, cultivar and harvest year. Those details tell you what you are getting, as the Yame name alone does not.
history: Little is documented about when black tea making began in Yame or who first made it known. It belongs to the wider group of Japanese-made black teas.
